_: The massed army (tools/army_spike.gd, scripts/army_vat.gdshader read it through data.gd; docs/TUNING.md). regiment: men in one regiment (one draw). frontages: men abreast a regiment may stand (each regiment picks one: lines and columns, not one square). man: the soldier's height in world units (the realm's people stand ~0.22). spacing.file, spacing.rank: units between men abreast and front to back. jitter.place, jitter.turn, jitter.size: how far a man stands off his mark, turns off the line (radians), and differs in size (share). gap: units between regiments. muster.clear: units kept clear round the seat's centre; muster.reach: how far out the field may run; muster.slope: the most a regiment's ground may rise across it; muster.keepOff: no road or track within this share of a regiment's width of its middle (0.75 takes in its corners, turned a little), and the trees within it are counted and felled; muster.treeCost: what a tree on the field costs against a field one cell less compact (open fields win, a wooded seat still musters its host together, felling the trees); muster.nearCost: what a cell further from the seat costs. camera.tilt: degrees the army shot's lens sits below the map view's own pitch (a low oblique; negative is lower); camera.quarter: radians the host turns off square to the lens, so faces and colours show. march.share: the share of regiments still marching in to the muster; march.from: how far back (units) they start, low and high; march.speed: units a second. stance: the share of standing regiments at the ready (shields up) instead of at ease. albedo: the kit's paint brightness under the realm's sun. team.rects: up to four KayKit palette cells (u0, v0, u1, v1, and how much of it takes the colour, 1 when left out) that wear the house colour: the red cloth swatches (only 3.5% of the knight's surface, so a regiment read plain grey) his helmet's cell at 0.5 (from the oblique view a regiment is mostly helmets) and his breastplate's steel cell (34% of him), painted in the house colour at 0.65; team.shade: the colour's brightness over the swatch's own light.
